title: Manifold-Aware Perturbations for Constrained Generative Modeling
claim: Perturbing data only along the normal directions of a constraint manifold recovers the original distribution better than isotropic noise.
layout: 2×5 grid, left-to-right pipeline per row, L1 errors beneath final columns
description: A 2×5 grid of toy examples. The rows are a line manifold (reach = ∞) and a spiral manifold (reach = 0.236). The columns are Original Density, Isotropic Noise, Normal-Only Noise, Iso → Projected, and Normal → Projected. The original density is a thin curve colored with a purple-to-yellow heatmap. Isotropic noise appears as a diffuse blue point cloud around the black manifold. Normal-only noise shows orange arrows perpendicular to the manifold, with the cloud spread along those directions. The two right-hand columns show the projected densities. Orange L¹ error text marks the isotropic result (0.248 for the line, 0.105 for the spiral). Purple L¹ error text marks the normal-only result (0.000 for the line, 0.058 for the spiral). The eye goes to the colored error numbers at the bottom right, which show that the normal-only approach is better.
caption: An illustration of our proposed manifold-aware perturbation and comparison to isotropic perturbations showing exact recovery for linear manifolds and lower error for the spiral dataset.
abstract: Generative models have enjoyed widespread success in a variety of applications. However, they encounter inherent mathematical limitations in modeling distributions where samples are constrained by equalities, as is frequently the setting in scientific domains. In this work, we develop a computationally cheap, mathematically justified, and highly flexible distributional modification for combating known pitfalls in equality-constrained generative models. We propose perturbing the data distribution in a constraint-aware way such that the new distribution has support matching the ambient space dimension while still implicitly incorporating underlying manifold geometry. Through theoretical analyses and empirical evidence on several representative tasks, we illustrate that our approach consistently enables data distribution recovery and stable sampling with both diffusion models and normalizing flows.
